analysis.title: Copper's Growth Signal Muddled By AI, Rates Stress
key_insights: Copper's role as a growth barometer is weakening. Its correlation with ISM Manufacturing PMI is 0.25 with an R-squared of 0.06, so the relationship is largely non-deterministic.

Copper's correlation with the AI equity trade is near a three-year cycle high, and its sensitivity to rates volatility has become more negative. Demand expectations are tied to data-center construction, electrification and semiconductor investment.

Rising real yields and rates volatility have tightened credit conditions, which threatens the capital-intensive AI investment cycle. Stress in lower-quality credit and weaker investment expectations could pressure AI equities and spill into copper before physical demand adjusts.

China accounts for about 56% of global refined copper demand. Property sector weakness, choppy industrial activity and a declining credit impulse are headwinds, even though the copper premium trades near record highs on post-Golden Week restocking.
Structural demand from electrification and AI infrastructure may not be enough to offset weaker Chinese demand and a higher cost of capital.

Copper implied volatility is near one-year lows, so the market is not pricing a decisive directional move despite macro uncertainty. Low volatility does not imply an imminent selloff, but leaves copper exposed to repricing.
The author argues the balance of risks favors tightening financial conditions over resilient growth, and that copper's growing financial-market beta may be a liability at this point in the cycle.
